answer: Ridge-and-Reef Reputation Depth**. Each identity must accumulate a minimum depth of verified interactions, scored on a weighted ridge where recent actions count less than settled history; new identities start at zero. To act as N agents, an attacker must furnish N times the genuine interaction volume, plus pay an unrecoverable comet-delay cost: each action is held until its score matures, stalling coordination for the full maturation window. Sybils therefore buy both volume and time, and the marginal per-identity cost stays constant rather than falling with scale.
